text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — latency regression detected for hosted API (p95 increase) — severity: high. Alert rule: latency-regression-prod. Notified: @sre_jen, @roxanne, @eng-runtime-lead

sre_jen: Acknowledge. I'm on it, grabbing context. Which customers affected? any spike in error rate?

roxanne: Seeing p50 from ~60ms -> 120ms, p95 from ~220ms -> 480ms across model-serving-prod cluster us-west-2. Error rate stable (2xx), just slow tails. Customer success flagged 3 customers experiencing timeouts at client side.

mike: Adding traces from yesterday -> today window. Quick check: deploy-bot shows a system kernel update rolled to some hosts ~02:10 UTC (linux-5.19.12 -> 5.19.15) and a runtime binary patch to attention-kernel applied ~02:25 UTC to pool-gpu-1. Could be correlated.

ida: I'm on-call handoff in 10m, will join immediately. Roxanne if you own mitigation please call it out so I can take next steps after handover.

ezra: Pulling perf counters and flamegraphs from host-32, host-41 which show long scheduler wait in worker threads. Attaching a short sample: ```
# perf top sample (host-32)
cpu 0-7, workload: inference
Top symbols:
  12.5%  runtime_kernel.o runtime_attention_forward
   9.2%  libc-2.31.so memcpy
   8.0%  kernel: __do_softirq
   6.7%  runtime_kernel.o kv_cache_lookup
```

eng-runtime-lead: Good detail. That memcpy jump suggests cache-line misses or changed allocator path. Any change in quantization or kernel selection?

ml-perf: We rolled a micro-optimization in runtime to use a new tiled attention kernel flagged as opt/tile-3 last night. It was intended to lower latency for long sequences. Could regress on short sequences if the kernel selection heuristic misfires.

roxanne: Hypothesis 1: kernel selection heuristic now picks tiled attention for many short requests -> higher per-op overhead causing p95 spike. Hypothesis 2: Recent host kernel update changed scheduler behaviour causing increased preemption and context switches.

ida: Immediate mitigation: can we force runtime to fallback to baseline attention kernel for the affected pool? If yes, we can revert selection policy without a full rollback.

eng-runtime-lead: Yes — configuration flag runtime.attention.force_kernel=baseline can be toggled via config service. I'm patching a canary to host-32/41 now. Command I used: ```
# toggle config (canary)
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://config.internal/v1/patch -d '{"pool":"pool-gpu-1","runtime":{"attention":{"force_kernel":"baseline"}}}'
```

incident-bot: change applied to pool-gpu-1 (canary hosts: host-32, host-41) by eng-runtime-lead at 1865008896. Monitoring...

roxanne: After canary flip: p95 on host-32 dropped from 510ms -> 230ms within 30s. Good signal. rolling to rest of pool now.

mike: Rolling to remaining hosts in pool-gpu-1. Also triggering traffic migration for mission-critical customers to dedicated-pool until full rollout completes.

customer-success: Notified customers A,C,D about mitigation and migration. They're seeing improved latencies for requests routed to dedicated-pool.

ida: Handoff: @ida taking lead. @sre_jen monitoring cluster health and rollback window.

sre_jen: Confirming error rates normal, CPU and GPU utilization stable. Token costs unaffected. Will start collecting timelines and logs for RCA.

eng-runtime-lead: Rollout completed at 1865008908. p95 cluster-wide returned to ~240ms. Marking incident mitigated (traffic stabilized).

roxanne: Now transitioning to RCA. We need timeline, scope, root cause, and action items. I'll start timeline notes here.

roxanne: Timeline (UTC):
- 02:08: kernel update batch started on subset of hosts (linux 5.19.12 -> 5.19.15)
- 02:25: runtime opt roll (opt/tile-3) promoted to pool-gpu-1
- 02:42: alert fired: latency-regression-prod
- 02:44: incident bot paged SREs
- 02:50: canary kernel toggle to baseline applied to host-32/41
- 02:52: p95 improved on canary hosts
- 02:55: rollback of kernel selection to baseline for pool completed
- 03:00: traffic migration for 3 customers to dedicated-pool completed

ida: Scope: Impacted hosted API routes for short-sequence generation (<=64 tokens) on pool-gpu-1 in us-west-2. Estimated p95 regression ~+200-250ms for those paths. No increased 5xx. Customers affected: 3 reported, internal telemetry shows ~0.6% of requests experienced >400ms extra latency.

ezra: Evidence linking to kernel and runtime change: hosts with only kernel change but not runtime opt showed smaller regressions (~+40ms) vs hosts with runtime opt enabled saw +250ms. Perf counters: increase in context-switches and LLC-misses when tiled kernel used on short sequences. Sample perf output: ```
# perf stat -e context-switches,cycles,cache-misses -p <pid> -- sleep 10
   12,532      context-switches
  1,234,123,456      cycles
    34,512      cache-misses # 0.0028% of accesses
```

ml-perf: Kernel selection code missed a heuristics boundary: seq_len_threshold default was 64 but we had an off-by-one in policy evaluation so many seq=48-64 selected tiled. Patch landed in opt/tile-3. Reproduced locally with short seq input: tiled path adds ~180ms overhead due to setup+matmul tiling overhead dominating for small mats.

eng-runtime-lead: Confirmed. Also noted libc memcpy contribution where tiled kernel copies extra buffers. That's exacerbated by kernel scheduler changes increasing preemption window. Combined effect produced the observed p95 uplift.

roxanne: Root cause (draft): Change in runtime kernel selection (opt/tile-3) caused tiled attention kernels to be chosen for short sequences; the tiled kernel has higher fixed setup cost and extra memcpy, producing higher tail latency. Kernel update may have amplified latency by altering scheduling/preemption behaviour on affected hosts.

ida: Action items: (assign owners)
- Rollback or adjust heuristic: set seq_len_threshold to 80 to avoid selecting tiled for short sequences (ml-perf).
- Add unit/integration perf tests that run tiled vs baseline across seq length grid to catch regressions (ml-perf + eng-runtime).
- Add automated monitoring anomaly: detect sudden rise in memcpy or cache-miss counters per worker (sre_jen + eng-infra).
- Harden canary gating: require p95 regression check for short-sequence synthetic load before promotion (eng-runtime-lead).
- Investigate kernel update scheduling: evaluate kernel tuning flags and pause auto-kernel-batch for gpu hosts until validated (eng-infra + eng-sre).

mike: I'll create a patch PR to bump threshold and add a perf test in the CI perf-suite. PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3124

ml-perf: I'll prepare a reproducible perf job and add it to nightly perf runs. Also adding a microbench harness to measure fixed setup overhead of tiled kernel.

eng-runtime-lead: Adding a quick guard to runtime to prefer baseline kernel when request.seq_len <= 80 until we ship a proper fix. Will deploy to staging and then to prod with canary gating.

customer-success: Customers notified of mitigation and RCA draft. Asking for written summary for external comms after RCA is finalized.

roxanne: Postmortem notes: Severity high, but no data loss and quick mitigation possible. We should target a CL by EOD with fix + perf tests.

ida: Will schedule a 30m follow-up postmortem meeting at 09:00 UTC to finalize owners and timeline.

eng-runtime-lead: One more note: captured trace span snippet from request that hit p95: ```
Span: request-root -> runtime.exec -> attention.select_kernel -> tiled_attention.init (120ms) -> tiled_attention.matmul (40ms) -> memcpy (60ms) -> postprocess (10ms)
Total server time: ~250ms (expected ~70ms)
```

sre_jen: Saving logs and perf artifacts to s3://redwood-incident-archive/1865008888/. Commands used: ```
# collect perf + traces
sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60
scp host-32:/var/tmp/perf.data s3://redwood-incident-archive/1865008888/host-32-perf.data
```

incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated at 1865008909. Runbook: continue RCA thread and mark postmortem in postmortems channel when ready.

roxanne: Thanks everyone. I'll draft the RCA doc and share. If anyone has additional trace spans or perf data drop them in the s3 folder. :thumbsup:

ida: Closing handoff: I'll remain the action-owner till fixes merge. Leaving thread but will monitor. :eyes:
